# My Thinking

I am 73 years old. My back is not what it used to be, and there are only two of us in the house. I have worked this land for 50 years and I know this soil. I know the wells, the weather, the pests. I do not need to experiment.

**On the land split:** Stevia is my main business now. The stevia company in the county sends a truck to collect, and the price is more stable than cotton. Cotton picking is brutal labor for old bones. I will put 4 mu into stevia and keep only 1.5 mu in cotton — enough to sell a bit and have some flexibility, but not so much that I ruin my back at harvest.

**On stevia:** I have been growing it long enough to know the cuttings schedule. I will do two harvests — one in midsummer, one in early autumn — and push the potassium up a bit because that helps with the glycoside content the buyers want. I will not overfeed nitrogen or the leaves get too leafy and the sweetness drops. Water after each cutting, otherwise the new growth wilts. I spray only when I see aphids or whitefly — not on a fixed calendar, I can still tell by looking.

**On cotton:** I keep it simple. I have grown cotton here since I was in my twenties. I use the improved Bt variety — less spraying for bollworm. I do my base fertilizer before planting, topdress at boll-setting stage, and I water at the five critical times I have always known: seedling establishment, squaring, flowering, boll formation, boll opening. I spray when I see pests, not preventively.

**On tillage:** I use the rotary tiller I rent from the village. Deep ploughing is too hard now. The rotary is enough — I have built up this soil for decades, it does not need to be torn apart.
